title: Late-arriving facts: a reprocessing window that keeps totals right
objective_text: Fold a batch of late and retried events into a daily aggregate by recomputing only the days the batch touches, without double counting and without losing days whose detail has been archived.
scenario: Tills sometimes upload events a day or two late, and the uploader retries when it times out. daily_sales feeds the morning dashboard. The events table only keeps recent detail; older days exist only as totals in daily_sales, so a full rebuild would wipe them.
verifies: Your SQL ran on this PC with DuckDB; daily_sales has the right total for every day, old days are untouched, and the retried event counts once.
does_not_verify: That the SQL runs unchanged in Spark SQL or a Fabric Warehouse.
Streaming watermarks in Spark structured streaming, which solve the same problem for streams (see E26 and E42).

expected.result: The starter's final SELECT over daily_sales, ordered by sale_date.

validation.fail: Check 1 and 2 May (no detail any more), 4 May (a retried event) and 6 May (a new day).

hints: Rebuilding daily_sales from events loses 1 and 2 May: their events are archived. Recompute only the days in stg_events.
First add the batch to events, skipping event_ids that are already there (e3 is a retry).
DELETE the affected days from daily_sales, then INSERT them again from events grouped by event_date.
explanation: Late data means an aggregate that was right yesterday is wrong today. The safe pattern is a reprocessing window: find the periods the new batch touches, delete those periods from the aggregate and recompute them from the detail. Adding the batch's totals to the existing rows double counts retries; rebuilding everything loses periods whose detail has aged out and costs more every day. Deduplicating events by their id before aggregating makes the step safe to retry.
reset: Reset restores events, daily_sales and stg_events.
